=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1473-1523 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: When `review_rb_judge_dispatch.yml` cannot be dispatched, `_mt_dispatch_rb_judge` falls back to `_mt_dispatch_review`, which never passes `force_rb_judge=true`; core-profile consumers do not install that workflow, so a judge-decision grant never reaches the judge's merge path.
  WHY: The plain review dispatch is either skipped (`AUTOFIX_GATE_SKIP reason=terminal_same_head`, bypassed only when `FORCE_RB_JUDGE=true`) or runs a full review round, which G3 forbids. The lease then sits idle for up to MERGE_LEASE_IDLE_MINUTES (default 60) until `revoked_no_head_gate`, even though ai-review.yml and internal-review.yml already accept `force_rb_judge` (reviewer rated MAJOR).
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1892-1932 (with scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:3340-3351) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: A holder granted via `gate=judge_decision` still has `ai-review/head-gate` pending. `_merge_lease_pr_eligible`'s holder path returns `no_head_gate` once MERGE_LEASE_IDLE_MINUTES (default 60) has elapsed, without checking the judge-decision status or CI activity, so the tick revokes it with `revoked_no_head_gate` and records `skip=<pr>:<head>`.
  WHY: A judge run that is queued or slow past the 60-minute grace leaves the PR skip-listed on its unchanged head, which brings back the stall #9987 set out to fix. Severity disagreement: gemini and luna rated MAJOR, sonnet and glm rated NIT (out of scope: holder rules are a non-goal under #9983); the highest is used.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1510-1523 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `_mt_dispatch_rb_judge` does not write `rb-judge:<pr>` to the _CONFLICT_DISPATCH_TRACKER, so the judge can be dispatched more than once in the same cycle.
  WHY: Stall recovery could trigger a second judge dispatch in the same cycle, which wastes resources and could produce duplicate judge decisions (reviewer rated NIT).
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:3333-3361 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The default `*)` arm of `_merge_lease_pr_eligible` applies the judge-decision substitution to any head-gate state other than a trusted-login success/failure/error, including a `success` from an unrelated login; README.md:164 and agents.d/9987-judge-decision-lease-grant.md document it only for "head-gate is still pending or absent".
  WHY: Nothing fails at runtime: the judge-decision signal is still trusted-login and head-bound, and nothing in the pipeline produces that input today. It is spec-vs-code drift (both reviewers rated NIT).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: G3: "After the grant, the PR reaches a merge or a normal lease release without a person. The granted holder is taken through the judge's merge path ... It must not end in another review round that only labels the PR `ai:review-blocked` again and waits for stall recovery."
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_merge_train.sh::_mt_dispatch_rb_judge (fallback branch, lines 1516-1522) and the supported consumer workflow profiles under workflow-templates/profiles/
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: A failed `gh workflow run review_rb_judge_dispatch.yml` falls back to `_mt_dispatch_review` (scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1516-1522), which never passes `force_rb_judge=true`, even though workflow-templates/ai-review.yml line 39 and .github/workflows/internal-review.yml line 27 accept it; workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt omits review_rb_judge_dispatch.yml (only standard.txt and full.txt carry it), and tests/test_audit_consumer_drift.py:1027-1029 asserts this; tests/test_merge_lease.py `test_failed_judge_dispatch_falls_back_to_one_review_dispatch` and tests/test_review_merge_train.py `test_failed_judge_dispatch_falls_back_to_the_review_dispatch` lock in the review-round outcome; so G3 holds only for standard and full profile consumers.
- requirement: (Residual risk, out of scope per the issue) A holder granted via `gate=judge_decision` reaches the merge gates within `MERGE_LEASE_IDLE_MINUTES` (default 60); holder rules are a non-goal tracked under #9983 (PR #9985).
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_merge_train.sh::_mt_merge_lease_tick and _mt_merge_lease_tick_multi, holder revocation branch at scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1892-1896
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The holder still has `ai-review/head-gate` pending, and `_merge_lease_pr_eligible` revokes it with `revoked_no_head_gate` once `now - since >= MERGE_LEASE_IDLE_MINUTES`, then adds it to `MERGE_LEASE_SKIPS` with its current head. The reviewer asks the editor to confirm that the holder rules in PR #9985 cover this path.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:_mt_dispatch_rb_judge, lines 1510-1523; _mt_dispatch_review lines 1473-1496 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When the judge dispatch fails, the code falls back to a plain review dispatch that carries only `-f pr_number` and `-f allow_workflow_edits`. Core-profile consumers do not install `review_rb_judge_dispatch.yml`, so this fallback is their only path, and it never reaches the judge's merge path. On a head with a terminal marker it is skipped (scripts/review_autofix_step_evaluate_gate.sh lines 416-421, 607-611, `AUTOFIX_GATE_SKIP reason=terminal_same_head` unless `FORCE_RB_JUDGE=true`); otherwise it runs a full review round. The lease then sits idle until `revoked_no_head_gate` and `skip=<pr>:<head>`.
  WHY: workflow-templates/ai-review.yml (lines 39, 69) and .github/workflows/internal-review.yml (lines 27, 67) already accept and forward `force_rb_judge`, but the fallback never sets it. Suggested fix: first try `gh_retry gh workflow run "${wf}" --repo "${MT_REPO}" -f pr_number="${mt_rbj_pr}" -f force_rb_judge=true` on each wrapper, then fall back to `_mt_dispatch_review`.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:_mt_merge_lease_tick holder block, lines 1892-1896 and 1927-1932; scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh `_merge_lease_pr_eligible` holder branch, lines 3340-3351 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: A holder granted through `gate=judge_decision` has head-gate pending and is revoked with `revoked_no_head_gate` and skip-listed if the judge has not posted head-gate within MERGE_LEASE_IDLE_MINUTES. The holder check runs before the CI-aware idle test.
  WHY: A judge run that starts or finishes later than the 60-minute default brings back the stall. Holder revocation rules are a non-goal (#9983), so this is residual risk.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: G3: "After the grant, the PR reaches a merge or a normal lease release without a person. The granted holder is taken through the judge's merge path ... It must not end in another review round that only labels the PR `ai:review-blocked` again and waits for stall recovery."
  Expected change site: scripts/review_merge_train.sh `_mt_dispatch_rb_judge` (fallback branch, lines 1521-1522)
  Evidence of absence: The `core` profile does not install review_rb_judge_dispatch.yml (workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt). The fallback `_mt_dispatch_review` never passes `force_rb_judge=true`, although workflow-templates/ai-review.yml line 39 and .github/workflows/internal-review.yml line 27 accept it. Tests (tests/test_merge_lease.py `test_failed_judge_dispatch_falls_back_to_one_review_dispatch`, tests/test_review_merge_train.py `test_failed_judge_dispatch_falls_back_to_the_review_dispatch`) lock in the review-round outcome.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- HARDENING: scripts/review_merge_train.sh _mt_dispatch_rb_judge fallback (lines 1521-1522): before `_mt_dispatch_review`, dispatch ai-review.yml and internal-review.yml with `-f pr_number=<n> -f force_rb_judge=true`, log `MERGE_TRAIN_DISPATCHED ... workflow=<wf>`, and return 0. Estimated 6-8 lines; HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3.
- Pass-1 note: a head-gate `success` from a non-pipeline login falling into the default case is real but changes no runtime outcome, so it was not re-reported.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
